channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies at 65
item.description:
Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor has died at 65.
Taylor died on Monday, according to a joint statement from his family and former bandmates that was shared on Duran Duran's official website on Wednesday. The statement said Taylor "passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by his family," after a "long and courageous battle with prostate cancer."

item.title: Kushner: Israel needs to move beyond constant wartime mindset
item.description: Jared Kushner defends Trump's Gaza peace plan, blames Palestinian governance for obstacles to a two-state solution and urges Israel to focus on economic diplomacy.

item.title: Tragedy in Ma'ale Adumim: Two-year-old toddler dies after fall
item.description: A two-year-old toddler suffers a severe head injury after falling from a height while playing. Doctors at Hadassah Ein Kerem Hospital were to pronounce him dead.

item.title: Make peace, but not at the expense of Torah Principles
item.description: Peace and negotiations yes, but the red liines must be clear.

item.title: The prophecy of the Bnai Anousim's return
item.description: Five centuries after their ancestors were torn away from our people, the descendants of the Anousim are finding their way back, as Obadiah's prophecy predicted.

item.title: The three ways to describe Hashem
item.description: Our actions should reflect each one of those ways.

item.title: Tehran - brokers of death
item.description: Whoever takes that first photograph may never learn who will use it or why. Tehran is building a capability that reaches beyond its ideological base. Op-ed.

item.title: Unusual accident on Jerusalem light rail
item.description: A pedestrian's leg became trapped between a Jerusalem light rail car and the platform. Firefighters freed her using specialized equipment.

item.title: New Jersey Governor declares emergency as Thanksgiving storm approaches
item.description: New Jersey declares a statewide emergency ahead of a Thanksgiving storm expected to bring heavy rain, 60 mph wind gusts, and coastal flooding.

item.title: Amit Segal charges: "The media is acting criminally"
item.description: Segal claims that the flaws in the cases against Netanyahu were known in advance and calls on the court to examine the responsibility of those who led the proceedings.

item.title: Deadly explosion in Giza leaves highway engulfed in flames, 30 dead
item.description: At least 30 people were killed and 15 injured after a truck carrying petroleum products overturned and exploded in Egypt, engulfing vehicles in flames.

item.title: Senior political source warns: "Israel is returning to the laboratory, a reckless gamble"
item.description: A political source believes that Shas joining the government of change could jeopardize its political future and warns of the price Israel would have to pay for relying on Arab parties.

item.title: 'Wings instead of legs' | After losing both legs, he found a new mission
item.description: Rabbi Liraz Zeira, who was seriously wounded in Syria and lost both legs, recounts his struggle to survive, the faith that gave him strength and his dream of running again.

item.title: Iran denies chemical weapons program following Israeli minister's warning
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denies chemical weapons development and accuses Israel of seeking to draw the US into another war.

item.title: Trouble in anti-Netanyahu bloc | Liberman to get Justice Ministry; Golan furious
item.description: Yisrael Beytenu will receive the defense, justice, and immigration and absorption portfolios. Eisenkot is planning a government with fewer ministers, stirring resentment among his fellow bloc members.

item.title: NYC lawmakers demand investigation after event featuring Hillel canceled
item.description: Three NYC council members demand a civil rights investigation after a Hunter College event was canceled amid controversy over Hillel's participation.

item.title: Despite trial development | Netanyahu will not withdraw pardon request
item.description: Despite the judges' proposal to drop the bribery charge in Case 4000, Netanyahu does not currently intend to withdraw the pardon request he submitted to the president.

item.title: Hezbollah chief attacks Lebanese President, hails Iran as 'model of honor'
item.description: Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem accuses Lebanese President Joseph Aoun of deepening national divisions, defends Hezbollah's arms, and praises Iran.

item.title: Heading toward a trade war? | Trump's new tariff plan
item.description: The US president announced plans to impose new tariffs on at least 14 countries, including China, India, Japan and European Union member states.

item.title: Rabbi Haim Rettig opens up
item.description: The head of Ra'anana's hesder yeshiva calls for unity within religious Zionism and discusses military conscription for Haredim, his views on Bennett and his journey from secular school to leading a yeshiva.

item.title: Report: Yisrael Beytenu to receive Justice Portfolio
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot and Avigdor Liberman have agreed that the justice minister will be appointed from the Yisrael Beytenu party, Channel 13 News reported.

item.title: Saada predicts Netanyahu trial will end in full acquittal
item.description: MK Moshe Saada predicts an acquittal in Netanyahu's bribery case, levels serious accusations against law enforcement officials and says judges are giving the attorney general a chance to end proceedings before they write their verdict.

item.title: Houthi-launched projectile lands on Saudi port
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition reported on Wednesday evening that a projectile fired by the Houthi terrorist militia fell on Jazan Port in Saudi Arabia, causing minor damage but no civilian casualties. Efforts are underway to determine the type of projectile.

item.title: Netanyahu responds to trial developments: "Ten years of terrible suffering"
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivers a statement in response to developments in his trial and the judges' remarks that the prosecution should consider its next steps in two of the cases against him. Watch live

item.title: UNICEF aid boxes found at site where senior Hamas terrorist was killed
item.description: IDF reveals stacks of UNICEF aid boxes were found at the site where Hamas's northern Gaza internal security chief Muhammad Abu al-Aouf was killed.

item.title: The legal hurdle to compensation for terror victims
item.description: A court dismissed a NIS 5 million lawsuit against the PA. Attorney Yana Mano explains why proving a direct link between the policy of payments to terrorists and an attack makes it difficult for terror victims to obtain compensation.

item.title: Gotliv outlines path to ending Netanyahu's trial
item.description: MK Tally Gotliv explains why she believes the judges summoned the attorney general, proposes ending Netanyahu's trial without a plea bargain and calls for an investigation into the prosecution's conduct.

item.title: Shachar Ashkenazi missed Ishay Ribo's show, cried-and was surprised by his response
item.description: Musician and social media personality Shahar Ashkenazi missed an Ishay Ribo show she had booked for a break. Her tearful video went viral, and Ribo offered a new ticket. She told Arutz Sheva how her disappointment became a boost to her faith.

item.title: IDF Chief outlines 2027 plans to ease reserve duty and boost combat readiness
item.description: IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir says the military will seek to ease the burden on reservists in 2027 while increasing readiness for renewed combat.

item.title: Likud appeals election results
item.description: Likud has petitioned the Jerusalem District Court, seeking a review of the election results and the invalidation of results from polling stations where irregularities were found.
